findings.title: Failed load can wipe a cache another goroutine just filled
findings.body: GetWebAssets drops the read lock and later takes the write lock without re-checking entryPointAssetsCache. Every caller that observed a nil cache therefore reloads and then unconditionally assigns entryPointAssetsCache = result. If one of those loads succeeds and a later one fails, result is nil and the assignment clears the good cache. Later non-dev callers then miss the cache and fail (or stampede the manifest read again) even though a valid EntryPointAssets was already published. Only store the pointer when err == nil and the cache is still empty (or always keep the previous value on error), and repeat the nil check after Lock.

findings.title: Exclusive lock held across manifest I/O
findings.body: After the fast-path check, GetWebAssets holds entryPointAssetsCacheMu for the whole readWebAssetsFromFile / CDN path, including os.Open and JSON decode (and http.DefaultClient.Do if the CDN branch is ever enabled). In non-dev that stalls every other GetWebAssets caller on cold start; in dev the early return is skipped so every call takes this exclusive lock and concurrent page renders serialize on disk I/O. Load into a local variable without the mutex, then lock only to publish the pointer.
